## Global Instructions

# AGENTS.md — webgrip/workflows

The workflow catalogue is in [`README.md`](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/workflows/src/branch/main/README.md) and the decisions are in
[`docs/adrs/`](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/workflows/src/branch/main/docs/adrs); neither is repeated here. This file carries what an agent cannot
derive by reading a single workflow file: the two-tree contract, and the rules that look like
style and are not.

## The two trees

`.github/workflows/` is the **frozen source**. `.forgejo/workflows/` is its Forgejo-adapted
mirror (ADR 0002). Never hand-edit a generated file — edit the `.github/` original and
regenerate.

- [`scripts/generate-forgejo-workflows.sh`](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/workflows/src/branch/main/scripts/generate-forgejo-workflows.sh) copies each
  `.github/workflows/*.yml` into `.forgejo/workflows/` through a single `sed` that rewrites
  self-references `webgrip/workflows/.github/` → `webgrip/workflows/.forgejo/`. That sed is the
  whole adaptation a "mechanical" (Tier-1) copy gets. The script writes only under `.forgejo/`
  and never touches `.github/`.
- The **26 files in the `MANUAL[]` array are hand-owned** — registry pinning, auth, and the
  Forgejo reimplementations of GitHub-only workflows. The generator skips them. Adding a
  workflow that needs any real adaptation means adding it to `MANUAL[]` and porting it by hand,
  not loosening the generator.
- After generating, the script greps every generated file for
  `actions/checkout@v6|create-github-app-token|@semantic-release/github|ghcr\.io` and fails if
  one leaked. A hit is the signal that the file belongs in `MANUAL[]`.
- [`scripts/forgejo-parity-check.sh`](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/workflows/src/branch/main/scripts/forgejo-parity-check.sh) guards the layout from
  the other side: no orphan `.forgejo` workflow without a `.github` sibling, no forbidden
  construct in the mirror, and a coverage report of unported workflows. Workflows that are
  deliberately Forgejo-only (LAN-only Harbor, Cloudflare, the hard-gate families, this repo's
  own CI) must be listed in its `FORGEJO_ONLY` array with the reason, or the check reports them
  as orphans. Coverage is informational until `STRICT=1` or `.forgejo/.parity-complete`.

## `on_source_change.yml` and `on_docs_change.yml` are this repo's own CI

Every other file under `.forgejo/workflows/` is `on: workflow_call` — a library other repos
consume. These two are `on: push` and run **for** this repo. Do not read them as consumer
templates, do not mirror them into `.github/`, and do not "fix" their triggers to match the
library's shape.

## Load-bearing rules

- **`uses:` must be the `org/repo/path@sha` shorthand**, never a full `https://` URL. Forgejo
  resolves the called workflow's `runs-on` server-side, and a full URL leaves the job queued
  forever against an empty label list.
- **`actions/checkout@v5` is the default pin; `@v6`/`@v7` work too.** The old "v6 is broken on
  non-GitHub runners" rule was disproven on 2026-09-18 by a canary on the real Forgejo runner
  ([homelab-cluster run 1710](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/homelab-cluster/actions/runs/1710)):
  checkout v6 and v7 and setup-node v5, v6 and v7 all pass. Bump deliberately, never on automerge.
- **`WEBGRIP_CI_TOKEN`, never `secrets.FORGEJO_TOKEN`.** A caller-mapped secret of that name
  resolves to the runner's built-in per-job token, which cuts ghost releases attributed to
  Ghost, fires no native `release` event, and cannot write org packages.
- **The self-CI composite is referenced by remote pinned ref, not `./.forgejo/...`.** It runs
  its own `actions/checkout` as step one, so at `uses:` resolution time the workspace is still
  empty and a local path cannot resolve.
- **`runs-on: docker`.** The in-cluster Forgejo has one ephemeral runner pool and it advertises
  exactly that label.
- **A reusable workflow's inner jobs are flattened into the caller's graph, and the caller
  job's `if:` does NOT apply to them.** A "skipped" `uses:` still runs its jobs. Conditionals
  around reusable work must be step-level.
- **Releases are tag-only.** [`.releaserc.cjs`](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/workflows/src/branch/main/.releaserc.cjs) deliberately omits `manifest` —
  there is no version-bearing file to bump. `floatingMajorTag` is deliberately off: a moving
  `v1` would reintroduce the mutable ref the first tagging removed. Consumers pin immutable
  `@vX.Y.Z` and let Renovate move them.
- **Untagged is not a cosmetic problem.** Renovate resolves these refs through the
  `forgejo-tags` datasource, which looks refs up as tags: an `@main` pin 404s and fails the
  consumer's **entire** Renovate run, not just that dependency. The library shipped 45
  workflows with zero tags for months and broke every consumer this way.
- **Internal refs stay `webgrip/workflows/<path>@main` on main; the release pins them** (ADR 0007).
  Never write a relative `./` ref in a library file (Forgejo resolves it in the caller's repo) and
  never pin an internal ref to a tag or sha by hand: the release rewrites only `@main`, and
  `node scripts/internal-refs.cjs check` fails on anything else. A release tag points at a pin
  commit off main; `.releaserc.cjs` grafts those commits back so semantic-release still finds them.
- **The toolchain is the image** (ADR 0005). Release jobs run in
  `harbor.webgrip.dev/webgrip/semantic-release:<pin>` and install nothing at release time; the
  composite fails loudly without it rather than silently falling back.

## Repo rules

- **Comments are NOT allowed.** Always communicate intent with code: a precise name, a type, a
  smaller function, a test that states the case. A comment is a failure. This holds for every
  language in the repo, prose in YAML and TOML included. Machine-read directives stay, because the
  toolchain acts on them as syntax: `// @ts-check`, `eslint-disable`, `<!-- prettier-ignore -->`,
  `# syntax=`, `# renovate:`, `# yaml-language-server:`, and shebangs. Doc-comment forms the
  toolchain itself reads are not comments either and stay: godoc directly above an exported
  identifier, rustdoc `///` and `//!`, and PHPDoc blocks carrying type tags. Anything that outlives
  a single expression belongs in `docs/` or an ADR, where it gets reviewed, linked and kept
  current. The estate decision is
  [ADR 0006](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/workflows/src/branch/main/docs/adrs/0006-no-comments-in-code.md).

# webgrip baseline

These rules hold in every webgrip repository. The repository's own text outside this block wins where it disagrees.

- GitOps first: desired state lives in Git and Flux reconciles it. Change a manifest or values file instead of running `kubectl apply/patch/delete` or `helm install/upgrade`; reading is fine. A rollout is live only once the reconciled revision and the running image digest match.
- Secrets have a level, and OpenBao holds the only original ([homelab-cluster ADR-0055](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/homelab-cluster/src/branch/main/docs/techdocs/docs/adr/adr-0055-one-secrets-model-six-levels.md)). Never put a plaintext value in a file or add a `*.sops.yaml` outside the floor. Write the manifests and hand the person the `bao kv put` command; never handle the value. The `secrets-levels` skill places a secret and the `guard-secrets` hook enforces the floor.
- Follow the branching model the repository's `AGENTS.md` states; without one, commit to `main`. After a push, check the commit is on the remote (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/<branch>`). A forced update of a shared branch is an incident.
- Several sessions share one working tree. Commit only the paths you wrote (`git commit -- <paths>`), never `git add -A`, `git add .` or `git commit -a`, and expect any local commit to be pushed by another session at any moment ([shared working tree](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/agent-standards/src/branch/main/docs/shared-working-tree.md)).
- Run tools through mise (`mise exec -- <cmd>`); versions are pinned in `mise.toml`.
- Write Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `chore:`, `refactor:`) with an optional scope, one change per commit.
- Renovate owns dependency versions: review its pull requests instead of bumping what it manages.
- Reuse before building: generate, then reference (a pinned `uses:` or an `@webgrip` package), then sync pull requests, then a one-off copy ([reuse and releases](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/agent-standards/src/branch/main/docs/reuse-and-releases.md)).
- No comments in code. Carry intent in names, types, small functions and tests; reasoning goes to `docs/` or an ADR. Machine-read directives stay: shebangs, `# syntax=`, `# renovate:`, schema hints, `@ts-*`, `eslint-*`, `# shellcheck`, `# noqa`, `//go:*` and doc comments a tool reads ([ai-skills ADR-0001](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/ai-skills/src/branch/main/org/adrs/adr-0001-no-comments-in-code.md)).
- Deployable apps follow `application-template`; Helm plumbing comes from `common-charts` and `helm-dependency-values`. A ServiceMonitor or PrometheusRule needs `release: kube-prometheus-stack`, or it is never scraped.
- Docs are TechDocs (MkDocs under `docs/`) and change with the behaviour. Durable knowledge goes into the repository, skill or command that owns it, never into agent memory.
- Validate with the repository's documented gate before committing, and say plainly what failed or was skipped. Check the primary source before claiming something works or never worked.
- Never hardcode secret domains or IPs; template them. Escape runtime shell variables in manifests as `$${...}`, because Flux postBuild substitution eats `$`.
- Keep organisations apart: no names, hosts, ids or people of an employer or client in a webgrip repository.
- The Bash tool may run zsh: quote variables, use arrays, `set -o pipefail` before gating on a pipeline, and close stdin (`< /dev/null`) for CLIs that may read it.

## Files matching `.forgejo/**`

# Forgejo Actions

- Reference a reusable workflow in shorthand, pinned to a SHA: `uses: webgrip/workflows/.forgejo/workflows/<name>.yml@<sha> # vX.Y.Z`. A full `https://` URL leaves the job waiting forever for runner labels.
- An `if:` on a `uses:` job does nothing: Forgejo v15 flattens the called jobs and drops it. Gate inside the reusable workflow (`only-refs`, `enabled`) or give the calling job its own `runs-on`.
- Use `runs-on: docker`, the `Europe/Amsterdam` timezone (cron schedules too) and `@webgrip/semantic-release-config` for releases.
- Check that a GitHub Marketplace action works on forgejo-runner before proposing it ([Forgejo CI](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/agent-standards/src/branch/main/docs/forgejo-ci.md)).
